# aeneid-074 (X.185–275) — drafter's notes

39 units; `make_units.py` runs clean (no LINE COUNT / TOO LONG / NEWLINE / ENDING / NOTE LENGTH / MARK warnings). `t` comes
only from `A.cut`; no `sc`. Longest units are five lines (189–193, 219–223, 224–228a ending `adloquitur:`) and four lines
(185–188, 198–201a, 209–212, 231b–234a, 252–255, 272–275). Paragraphs 185, 198, 213, 215 all start a unit at line start and
carry `p: true`; each note opens "A new paragraph in Greenough." Note lengths 37–106 words.

Title `Duces Etrusci. Nympharum nuntius`; part "The Ship-Nymphs and the Blazing Shield (X.185–275)".

## Speech marks

- Cymodocea: “ 228 (`“Vigilasne`, unit 228b–229a) … ” 245 (`acervos.”`, unit 244–245).
- Aeneas's prayer: “ 252 … ” 255 (one unit, 252–255).
Counts of “ and ” match in t, l and i for every unit.

## Misprints

None found. No closing mark joined to the next word in this part (both speeches close at line end).

## Latin Library disagreements

- 186 `Cinyre` / `Cunare`: noted (name differs between editions).
- 214 `aera` / `aere`: noted; `aera` read as nominative plural of `aes` ("the bronzes", the prows) as a new subject; same
  sense either way. Kept as printed (construable, so not a 5b misprint).
- 240 `certast` / `certa est`: noted as Greenough's form = `certa est`.
- 251 `super adspectans` / `supera aspectans`: noted briefly, same sense.
- 253 `urbis` / `urbes`: noted; `urbis` must be nominative plural here (with `cordi`), an old plural form. See doubtful points.
- 256 `rubebat` / `ruebat`: noted (changes the picture: reddening vs. rushing on).
- 268 `puppes`/`puppis`, 271 `ignes`/`ignis`, 272 `siquando`/`si quando`: morphology/orthography, not noted (except that
  `siquando` is glossed as `si quando`).
No bracketed lines in this part. No advisory: ordinary battle preparation, no killing on stage.

## Doubtful points

- 186 `Cinyre`: vocative; English uses "Cinyras" (the familiar name), though `-e` points rather to a nominative in `-us`/`-es`.
  Reviewer may prefer another English form; the note only says the name differs between editions.
- 188 `crimen, Amor, vestrum`: plural `vestrum` with singular `Amor` explained as Love addressed with his fellow love-gods.
  A judgement call.
- 199 `Tusci… amnis` identified as the Tiber.
- 202–203 the three races / four peoples of Mantua: note says Virgil does not name them and ancient commentators guessed.
- 214 `aera` as nominative (see above).
- 253 `urbis` as nominative plural: Greenough's `-is` is normally accusative; nominative `-is` is rare. If the reviewer judges it
  a misprint for `urbes`, rule 5b would apply; I kept the print as a doubtful reading and said what it must be.
- 261 `cum deinde… extulit` taken as inverted cum after `iamque`; `deinde` two syllables.
- 266 `clamore secundo` rendered "glad/joyful clamour".
- Scanner flags 217 (Aeneas) and 224 (`choreis`) are for the scan pass, not this draft.

## Attributions from memory (please verify)

- Ovid, Metamorphoses 2.367–380 for Cycnus's change into a swan (and the Heliades as poplars).
- Manto as daughter of Tiresias; Mantua named after her; Mincius flowing from Lake Benacus (Garda) past Mantua.
- Servius on `Vigilasne… vigila` as a ritual formula for waking the rex sacrorum by the Vestals (unchecked; reviewer may cut it).
- Cymodoce among the Nereids at Iliad 18.39; Cymodocea = "wave-receiver".
- Iliad 3.3–7, Trojans compared to cranes.
- Iliad 5.4–7, Athena kindles fire from Diomedes' helmet and shield.
- Iliad 22.26–31, Achilles like Sirius as Priam sees him.
- Triton's conch; Phaethon struck into the Eridanus/Po; Strymon cranes; Sirius and the dog days.
- Checked against the edition: Centaurus V.122; Pristis V.116; Cymodoce V.826; Aulestes XII.290; Palinurus lost and Aeneas
  steering V.867–868; ship-nymphs IX.77–122 (223 = IX.121 verbatim; vincula IX.118; genetrix IX.82, 117; promise IX.101–103;
  pines IX.80–92); Dindyma IX.618; Ignipotens VIII.414, 710; helmet `flammasque vomentem` VIII.620; `stans celsa in puppi`
  VIII.680 (Augustus at Actium); Aeneas at sea at midnight X.147.
